stated_limitation: CA1 serves as a negative control. ... only 4.5% in hippocampal CA1 (17/376) — statistically indistinguishable from the 5% false-positive rate of the permutation test, which validates the procedure. ... a modest, non-significant excess at 90° (11/14/24/12 units at 0/45/90/135°, chi² p ≈ 0.07)

justification.dataset: DANDI 000021 (Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels, drifting gratings) is the canonical dataset for orientation selectivity, with all relevant visual areas plus a hippocampal control present.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile, good units filtered, structures assigned by peak channel, invalid_times excluded, blank sweeps used for spontaneous baseline, spike counts via searchsorted on correct trial windows.
justification.analysis: gOSI as the 2θ resultant vector with blank subtraction, a proper 1000-shuffle permutation null, and CA1 as a negative control are exactly the right circular-statistics methods.
justification.correctness: Reported fractions (VISp 61/135, CA1 17/376, LGd 51/173) reproduce exactly from the committed CSV, are internally consistent, and the CA1 control matching the 5% chance rate confirms statistical soundness.
justification.figures: Rasters, tuning curves, population panels, heatmap, and permutation nulls are all clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, and example units are honestly chosen across the full selectivity range.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the evidence, the borderline 90° excess is explicitly flagged as non-significant, the control's meaning is stated, and single-session scope is disclosed with nothing overstated.
